19|## 1. Summary
20|
21|Fleet SRE is an agentic site reliability engineer for MSSPs running multi-tenant Google SecOps SOAR. It writes each service's monitoring contract, investigates when a tripwire fires, proposes a fix for a human to approve, and amends the contract when an incident exposes a gap. The platform underneath exists only to give it safe tools and deterministic checks.
22|
23|- **Problem.** An MSSP runs many tenants (SOAR environments) across many services in one instance. Connectors fail silently, a `LIVE` status can sit on a connector that ingests nothing, and each tenant's monitoring depends on who onboarded it.
24|- **What the SRE does.** Authors one contract per service version, investigates incidents with read-only tools, proposes allowlisted actions, writes the postmortem and drafts contract amendments.
25|- **Why it can be trusted.** It isn't. Deterministic code grades every output: contracts by a chaos scorecard, evidence when it is recorded, diagnoses when they are submitted, fixes by tripwires.
26|- **Fleet leverage.** Amendments land on the service contract, so one tenant's incident hardens every tenant on that service.
27|- **Built on.** A local-first Python system with a mock SecOps built against Google's published Chronicle API and SOAR log format, deployed to a personal GCP project (Cloud Logging, Pub/Sub, IAM, Cloud Run, Firestore).
28|- **Entry.** Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon, Indie track, "Build for Your World" theme. Submission due 2026-11-04 at 9:00 PM ET.
29|
30|## 2. Design principles
31|
32|1. **Verified, not trusted.** Every SRE output has a deterministic check: a contract must pass the chaos scorecard, evidence must exist when it is recorded, a diagnosis must rest on recorded evidence of the right kind, a fix must pass change-point tripwires.
33|2. **Reason once, run cheap.** The model works when a contract is written or amended and when an incident opens. No model sits in the watch loop.
34|3. **One contract per service.** The contract versions with the service definition. Per-tenant differences are parameters. The platform uses whatever integration version is installed; upgrades are a separate process.
35|4. **Every incident hardens every tenant.** Amendments land on the service contract, so a gap found on one tenant closes for all of them.
36|5. **The agent holds no credentials.** Read tools are proxied by the platform under a read-only identity; writes need human approval and run under a separate identity. IAM enforces this and tests prove it.
37|6. **Built against Google's spec.** Mock resources and log labels copy the published Chronicle API and SOAR logging docs, so the mock can be swapped for a real instance. What is invented is labelled as invented (see `mocks.md` §9).
38|7. **Local first.** Everything runs on a laptop with `make demo`. GCP services are adapters behind ports, swapped in late.
39|8. **The same rule applies to the build.** Humans write what defines correctness (contracts, scenarios, expected outcomes, acceptance test specs, SRE prompts in `prompts/`). The coding agent writes what is graded against them.
40|9. **Checks live inside the tools.** A gate runs inside the tool that moves work forward (recording evidence, submitting a diagnosis), never as a separate tool the model may choose to call, because a confident model skips optional checks. A refused call comes back as an error the model reads and fixes. The model chooses every call; code never hard-codes the order.
41|
42|Field lessons that shape the tripwires: absence-only detection cannot tell quiet from broken, and a field changing type (severity arriving as a string) passes every volume check.
43|
44|## 3. The SRE loop
45|
46|The model acts at three points (author, investigate, close). Deterministic code grades each output before anything changes; inside an investigation, the gates sit in the tools (§6.1).
47|
48|```mermaid
49|flowchart LR
50|  A["Write contract (SRE)"] --> B["Chaos scorecard"] --> C{"Passes?"}
51|  C -- "no: revise" --> A
52|  C -- "yes" --> D["Approve contract (human)"] --> E["Tripwires watch"]
53|  E -- "tripwire fires" --> F["Investigate (SRE)"]
54|  F -- "escalates or hits a limit" --> N["Needs input (human)"]
55|  N -- "reply, more turns, or fault state changed" --> F
56|  F -- "proposes action" --> G["Approve fix (human)"]
57|  G -- "rejected with notes" --> F
58|  G -- "approved" --> H["Apply fix (deployer identity)"] --> I{"Verified?"}
59|  F -- "no action: verify recovery" --> I
60|  I -- "no: retry, max 2, then escalate" --> F
61|  I -- "yes" --> J["Close incident (SRE postmortem)"]
62|  J -- "gap found: amend" --> A
63|```
64|
65|1. **Author.** Given a service brief, sample logs and parameters, the SRE drafts a contract. The harness scores it; the SRE revises against the scorecard (max 3 revisions); a human approves.
66|2. **Watch.** The evaluator runs every deployment's tripwires. No model call.
67|3. **Investigate.** A trip opens an incident. The SRE states hypotheses, investigates with read tools, records evidence that is checked as it is recorded, and submits a diagnosis through a gated tool (§6.1). The diagnosis proposes one action, proposes no action and asks for verification, or escalates.
68|4. **Hand off.** An escalation, or an investigation that hits a limit, pauses the incident at NEEDS_INPUT. No model calls are made while it waits. It resumes the same session only when something changed: a human replied, more turns were granted, or the incident's tripwire state changed (for example, a credential was rotated outside the platform).
69|5. **Approve and apply.** A human sees hypotheses, evidence and the patch diff, and approves or rejects with notes; notes go back to the SRE as its next message. On approval the executor journals its intent, then applies the change under the deployer identity.
70|6. **Verify.** A change-point window tightens checks on that component. The diagnosis states the expected outcome; the tripwires decide. Failure returns to investigation at most twice, then escalates.
71|7. **Close and learn.** The SRE writes a postmortem. If the incident exposed a gap (a late or missing trip), it drafts an amendment, which goes back through the scorecard and approval and then applies to every deployment of that service.

110|## 5. Contracts and tripwires
111|
112|A contract is one JSON file per service version. Deployments supply parameters only. Full schema: `contracts/schema.json` (D1).
113|
114|```json
115|{
116|  "service": "alert-ingestion",
117|  "version": "1.0.0",
118|  "parameters": {
119|    "expectedAlertsPerHour": { "type": "number", "required": true },
120|    "intervalSeconds": { "type": "integer", "required": true }
121|  },
122|  "components": [
123|    { "id": "connector", "kind": "connectorInstance",
124|      "logs": { "container_name": "python", "match": ["connector_name", "connector_instance"], "deploymentBy": "labels.connector_instance" } },
125|    { "id": "ingestion", "kind": "etlFlow",
126|      "logs": { "container_name": "etl", "match": ["correlation_id"], "deploymentBy": "jsonPayload.environment" } }
127|  ],
128|  "tripwires": [
129|    { "id": "dead-connector", "component": "connector", "type": "cadence",
130|      "spec": { "event": "connector.run.completed", "intervalSeconds": "${intervalSeconds}", "maxSilentIntervals": 3 } },
131|    { "id": "canary", "component": "ingestion", "type": "synthetic",
132|      "spec": { "everyMinutes": 10, "deadlineSeconds": 180 } },
133|    { "id": "priority-shape", "component": "ingestion", "type": "schema",
134|      "spec": { "event": "alert.ingested", "field": "jsonPayload.alert.priority", "type": "integer", "enum": [-1, 40, 60, 80, 100], "required": true, "consecutive": 1, "recoverAfter": 20 } },
135|    { "id": "connector-errors", "component": "connector", "type": "errorSignature",
136|      "spec": { "minSeverity": "WARNING", "windowRuns": 10, "threshold": 8 } }
137|  ],
138|  "changePoint": { "durationSeconds": 1800, "overrides": { "dead-connector": { "maxSilentIntervals": 2 } } },
139|  "provenance": { "authoredBy": "<model id>", "scorecard": "<run id>", "approvedBy": "<human>" }
140|}
141|```
142|
143|Values were settled in D1; `contracts/*.json` is authoritative and this example matches it. The `intel-sync` contract has one `jobInstance` component and three tripwires: `dead-job` (cadence on `job.run.completed`, 3 silent intervals), `hollow-run` (schema on `job.run.completed` entries whose `status` is `SUCCESS`: `jsonPayload.indicatorsSynced` ≥ 1, tripping after 3 consecutive violations and recovering after 2 valid runs) and `job-errors` (errorSignature, 2 ERROR runs in the last 3).
144|
145|**Contract rules settled in D1.**
146|
147|- `logs.deploymentBy` names the entry field that identifies the deployment: `labels.connector_instance` for connectors, and the invented `jsonPayload.environment` for jobs and ETL. Google's documented job label (`job_name`) names the job definition, which is the same on every tenant, and ETL entries carry only `correlation_id`.
148|- Cadence specs name their interval explicitly (`"intervalSeconds": "${intervalSeconds}"`).
149|- Schema tripwires take `event` (only entries with that `jsonPayload.event` are checked), `where` (equality filters on other fields), `consecutive` (violations in a row to trip; default 1) and `recoverAfter` (valid entries in a row to recover; default `consecutive`). Entries the filters exclude neither count nor reset either run.
150|- For `errorSignature`, a run is one `runId`, its severity is the worst entry in it, and it is judged when it completes (the component's cadence heartbeat). It trips when at least `threshold` of the last `windowRuns` runs are at or above `minSeverity`, and recovers after `windowRuns − threshold + 1` clean runs in a row.
151|- Entering a change point re-arms cadence from that moment: a heartbeat from before the change point never counts.
152|- Cadence goes by the latest heartbeat timestamp seen, not the last entry to arrive, and trips when the silence is strictly longer than `maxSilentIntervals × intervalSeconds`. It recovers on the first heartbeat that clears that condition.
153|- A canary seen exactly at its deadline is in time. A late canary does not recover the tripwire; the next canary seen in time does.
154|- `load_contract` rejects a bad contract with a `ContractError` code (table in `deliverables.md` §D1).
155|
156|| Tripwire type | Checks | Trips when | Failure it catches |
157|| --- | --- | --- | --- |
158|| `cadence` | A named heartbeat event (connector run, job run) against the deployment's interval | No event for N intervals | A stopped connector or job. Runs happen on schedule regardless of alert volume, so quiet tenants do not false-alarm |
159|| `synthetic` | A planted canary alert traced end to end by `correlation_id` | The canary misses its deadline | End-to-end breakage with a healthy-looking status |
160|| `schema` | Field presence, type and allowed values on ingested events | A required field is missing, the wrong type, or out of range | Silent type breakage that volume checks miss |
161|| `errorSignature` | WARNING/ERROR rate in a component's logs over the last N runs | Count ≥ threshold | A per-tenant credential Green Liar, without planting anything in the client's SIEM |
162|
163|**Canary scope.** In the demo the canary is planted in the fake upstream per tenant. In production, planting into a client's workspace is off the table, so the canary runs on one MSSP-owned canary tenant per service version (proves the code path), and `errorSignature` covers per-tenant credential failures.
164|
165|### 5.1 Chaos harness and scorecard
166|
167|- **Scenario library** (`fixtures/scenarios/<service>/*.yaml`, human-authored): fleet, duration, fault schedule, expected trips with a maximum detection latency, and `mustNotTrip`.
168|- **Replay**: the mock world generates each scenario's log stream on a `SimClock`; the stream runs through the evaluator. No GCP, seconds per run.
169|- **Scorecard**: per scenario, expected versus actual trips, detection latency, false positives. A contract passes only at 100% expected trips and zero false positives.
170|- **The SRE never writes scenarios or expected outcomes.** It sees scorecard results only.
171|- **Held-out scenarios.** Some scenarios are marked `holdout: true`. They never appear in revision feedback, not even by ID. A contract passes only if the holdouts pass too; when only a holdout fails, the feedback says "a held-out scenario failed" and nothing more. This stops the authoring loop from fitting the visible scenarios.
172|
173|## 6. The investigation: loop, tools, actions and gates
174|
175|### 6.1 The loop
176|
177|Each turn, the gateway sends the full history to the Meta Model API (Responses API, `store=False`, `parallel_tool_calls=False`, encrypted reasoning included and replayed; §8). The model returns one tool call; the platform runs it; the result, or the gate's refusal, goes back as the next input. The session is saved after every turn.
178|
179|- **One tool per turn.** A reply with no tool call gets "Plain text is not accepted. Call exactly one tool." and counts as a turn. If a response holds more than one call, only the first runs.
180|- **Last turn.** On the final turn the SRE is told to submit with what it has.
181|- **Rationale.** Every tool call carries a required `rationale` (at most 200 characters). The model's reasoning tokens are not readable (Chat Completions returns no `reasoning_content`; Responses returns it encrypted), so `rationale` is the visible "think" line in the trace and the UI timeline.
182|- **Ending.**
183|
184|| Ends with | Incident goes to | Model calls afterwards |
185|| --- | --- | --- |
186|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `propose` | AWAITING_APPROVAL | None until approval or rejection |
187|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `none` | VERIFYING | None |
188|| `submit_diagnosis` accepted, action `escalate` | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `escalated` | None until resumed |
189|| Three refused submissions | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `refused` | None until resumed |
190|| Turn limit | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `budget` | None until resumed |
191|| Token limit | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `token_budget` | None until resumed |
192|| The same call a third time | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `stuck` | None until resumed |
193|| Model API still failing after retries | NEEDS_INPUT, reason `model_unavailable` | None until resumed |
194|
195|- **Resume.** A NEEDS_INPUT incident resumes the same session (hypotheses and evidence kept) only when a human replied, granted more turns, or the incident's tripwire state changed since it paused. Otherwise resume is refused without a model call. What changed is the SRE's next message.
196|- **Gates off (evals only).** Gates can be switched off to measure what they catch; each verdict they would have given is still recorded. The incident manager and the web app refuse an investigator with gates off.
197|
198|### 6.2 Read tools (proxied, read-only identity)
199|
200|Every read tool also takes `rationale`. Reads are capped at 12 per session; a 13th read is refused with an error, and the loop continues.
201|
202|| Tool | Returns | Backed by |
203|| --- | --- | --- |
204|| `query_logs(deployment, window, filter)` | Log entries with `insertId` | `LogQuery` port |
205|| `get_resource(name)` | A connector instance, job instance, integration instance or environment | Mock Chronicle API `get` |
206|| `list_connector_logs(connectorInstance)` | Recent `ConnectorLog` records (empty unless log collection is on for that instance) | Mock `connectorInstances.logs.list` |
207|| `list_job_logs(jobInstance)` | Recent `JobInstanceLog` records | Mock `jobInstances.logs.list` |
208|| `test_integration_instance(name)` | Connectivity test result | Mock `integrationInstances.executeTest` (changes no state) |
209|| `compare_siblings(service, component, window)` | The same component's signals across every deployment of the service | Platform, computed |
210|| `tripwire_history(deployment)` | Recent trips, recoveries and approved changes | Platform state |
211|| `get_contract(service)` | Current contract and its last scorecard | Platform registry |
212|
213|### 6.3 Working tools and their gates
214|
215|The gates run inside these tools. A refused call returns `{"error": "...", "problems": ["..."]}` and never raises. Every tool result reaches the model as `{"callId": "...", "result": {...}}`, because the model cannot read call IDs back from the replayed history (D2 finding). A tool source's `field` is a dotted path into `result` (`successful`, not `result.successful`).
216|
217|| Tool | Does | Gate (inside the tool) |
218|| --- | --- | --- |
219|| `set_hypotheses(items)` | Sets 2–4 hypotheses, each with a statement and the evidence that would confirm it | 2–4 items; at least one marked `alternative: true` (a competing explanation, such as "this is fleet-wide, not specific to this tenant"). Required before `record_evidence` or `submit_diagnosis`. Calling it again replaces the set; evidence for removed hypotheses is dropped |
220|| `update_plan(plan)` | Records how the SRE will settle each hypothesis | None |
221|| `record_evidence(hypothesis, stance, source, why)` | Records one piece of evidence for (`supports`) or against (`refutes`) one hypothesis. `source` is `{insertId}` for a log entry or `{callId, field, value}` for a tool result | Log source: the `insertId` exists and belongs to the incident's deployment or to a sibling deployment the SRE queried in this session. Tool source: `callId` is a call made in this session and its result has `field` equal to `value`. The hypothesis exists. At most 3 items per hypothesis. Returns the evidence ID (`E1`, `E2`, …) and the hypotheses that still have no evidence |
222|| `submit_diagnosis(diagnosis)` | Submits the diagnosis (§6.5) | The submission rules in §6.5 |
223|
224|### 6.4 Action allowlist
225|
226|| Action | Notes |
227|| --- | --- |
228|| `connectorInstances.patch` | `updateMask` limited to `enabled`, `intervalSeconds`, `parameters` |
229|| `connectorInstances.restart` | Platform macro: patch `enabled=false`, then `enabled=true` |
230|| `connectorInstances.runOnDemand` | |
231|| `jobInstances.patch` | `updateMask` limited to `enabled`, `parameters` |
232|| `jobInstances.restart` | Platform macro: patch `enabled=false`, then `enabled=true` |
233|| `jobInstances.runOnDemand` | |
234|| `none` | No write: the fault has cleared (for example, after a human acted on an escalation). Goes straight to verification |
235|| `escalate` | Required when the fix is outside the allowlist (e.g. a credential rotation). Pauses the incident at NEEDS_INPUT |
236|
237|`connectorInstances.setLogsCollection` is not an action: turning on logging fixes nothing, so verification would fail it. The SRE can ask for it in an `escalationSummary`.
238|
239|### 6.5 Diagnosis schema and submission rules
240|
241|```json
242|{
243|  "incidentId": "string",
244|  "deployment": "string",
245|  "component": "string",
246|  "category": "connector_stalled | job_stalled | credential_failure | schema_drift | job_hollow_success | job_failing | unknown",
247|  "hypothesis": "ID of the hypothesis the SRE concludes (from set_hypotheses)",
248|  "summary": "the conclusion in one or two sentences",
249|  "evidence": ["E1", "E3"],
250|  "openQuestions": [ { "hypothesis": "string", "why": "string" } ],
251|  "action": {
252|    "type": "propose | none | escalate",
253|    "method": "one of the allowlist, when type is propose",
254|    "resource": "full resource name",
255|    "updateMask": ["field"],
256|    "patch": {},
257|    "escalationSummary": "string, when type is escalate"
258|  },
259|  "expectedVerification": { "tripwire": "string", "condition": "recovers_within", "seconds": 0 },
260|  "rollback": "string",
261|  "confidence": "low | medium | high"
262|}
263|```
264|
265|`category` is an enum so evaluations grade deterministically. The tool schema sets `additionalProperties: false` throughout.
266|
267|`submit_diagnosis` refuses a diagnosis, listing every problem, unless:
268|
269|1. **Schema.** It validates against the schema above.
270|2. **Recorded evidence only.** Every ID in `evidence` was recorded in this session.
271|3. **Hypothesis coverage.** The concluded hypothesis has at least one cited `supports` item. Every other hypothesis has at least one recorded `refutes` item or an entry in `openQuestions`.
272|4. **Category evidence rule.** The cited evidence includes what the category requires (table below).
273|5. **Action.** `propose`: the method is in §6.4, `updateMask` is within its allowed fields, and `resource` is the incident's component. `propose` and `none`: `expectedVerification.tripwire` is a tripwire of the incident's deployment. `none`: at least one cited item was recorded after the session's most recent resume. `escalate`: `escalationSummary` is not empty.
274|
275|After three refused submissions the incident goes to NEEDS_INPUT with reason `refused`.
276|
277|**Category evidence rules.** These check deterministically that the evidence is the right kind for the conclusion. They stand in for the model-judged "claims check" other agents use.
278|
279|| Category | Cited evidence must include |
280|| --- | --- |
281|| `connector_stalled` | The deployment's last `connector.run.completed` entry before the trip |
282|| `job_stalled` | The deployment's last `job.run.completed` entry before the trip |
283|| `credential_failure` | A WARNING or ERROR entry from the deployment's connector, and a `test_integration_instance` result with `successful: false` |
284|| `schema_drift` | An `alert.ingested` entry that violates the tripped schema tripwire |
285|| `job_hollow_success` | A `job.run.completed` entry with `indicatorsSynced: 0` |
286|| `job_failing` | A `job.run.error` entry, or a `job.run.completed` entry with `status: ERROR` |
287|| `unknown` | Nothing, but the action must be `escalate` |
288|
289|### 6.6 Guardrails
290|
291|- **Gates inside the tools** (§6.3, §6.5). Refusals are fed back to the model; nothing is retried silently.
292|- **Budgets.** Per investigation session: 24 turns, 12 read calls, 400,000 tokens (input plus output, configurable). Two remediation attempts per incident.
293|- **Stuck detection.** The same tool with the same canonical arguments (keys sorted, `rationale` excluded) a third time ends the session with reason `stuck`.
294|- **Concurrency.** The executor rejects a patch if the resource changed since the SRE read it.
295|- **Executor journal.** Append-only. Before any write the executor appends `intent` (approval ID, proposal hash, the resource version read at proposal time), then `started`, then `terminal` with the result. No write happens without a durable `intent` first. On restart, an `intent` without `terminal` is reconciled by re-reading the resource: if the change is already there it is marked done; otherwise it is applied once.
296|- **Recorded replay.** Live investigations chosen as fixtures (`fixtures/recorded/`) replay offline in CI through the scripted transport. Any difference in tool calls, gate verdicts or the final diagnosis blocks the merge.
297|- **Model calls.** Exponential backoff on 429; diagnoses cached on the public instance; spend caps.
298|- **Import boundary.** `fleetsre.sre` may not import GCP clients or the Chronicle client directly; it reaches the world only through the tool set.
299|
300|## 7. Identity and IAM
301|
302|| Identity | Grants | Must not be able to |
303|| --- | --- | --- |
304|| `obs-reader` (evaluator, SRE read tools) | `roles/logging.viewer`; `roles/pubsub.subscriber` on the one subscription; read permissions on the mock API | Write logs; call mock write methods |
305|| `deployer` (executor) | Write permissions on the mock API | Read the subscription; act without an approval record |
306|| `mock-soar` (mock SecOps runtime) | `roles/logging.logWriter` | Anything else |
307|| SRE (model) | None | Call GCP or the mock API directly |
308|
309|No service-account keys. Locally: impersonation. Cloud Run: attached service accounts. The mock verifies the caller's Google ID token and maps the service-account email to Chronicle-style permissions (`chronicle.connectorInstances.get`, `chronicle.connectorInstanceLogs.get`, ...). Tests: positive paths, negative 403s, exact permission sets via `testIamPermissions`, and no user-managed keys (`deliverables.md` D7).

311|## 8. Model usage
312|
313|One gateway, per-role config. Assignments are provisional until the D2 spike and the D5 live eval.
314|
315|| Role | Frequency | Starting model | Reasoning effort |
316|| --- | --- | --- | --- |
317|| Author / amend contracts | Rare | Muse Wonder via Meta Model API (model ID to confirm on the dashboard) | `high` |
318|| Investigate / propose | Per incident | `muse-spark-1.3` via Meta Model API | `medium` |
319|| Postmortem | Per closed incident | `muse-spark-1.3` | `low` |
320|| Fallback | On rate limits | Muse Spark Open from a partner, if credits arrive: Baseten `meta-models/muse-spark-open` (base URL `https://inference.baseten.co/v1`) or Fireworks `accounts/fireworks/models/muse-spark-open` | `medium` |
321|| Building the project | Throughout | Muse Code | — |
322|
323|**API details** (from Meta's cookbooks):
324|
325|- **Endpoint and key.** Base URL `https://api.meta.ai/v1`. The key lives in `MODEL_API_KEY` and is passed explicitly; the OpenAI SDK does not read that variable on its own.
326|- **Investigation loop.** Responses API with `store=False` and the full history sent every turn, `include=["reasoning.encrypted_content"]` so reasoning is replayed between turns, `parallel_tool_calls=False`, and `reasoning={"effort": ...}` per role. Effort levels: `none` < `minimal` < `low` < `medium` < `high` (`xhigh` is the same as `high`).
327|- **JSON outside tools** (authoring, postmortem). On the Responses API use `text.format` with a JSON schema; `response_format` returns HTTP 400 there. A recursive `$ref` also returns 400, so the schema given to the authoring model must be flattened.
328|- **Prompt caching.** Keep the stable prefix first (system prompt, tool specs, contract) and record `usage.input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` and `usage.output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens` in the transcript (field names confirmed in D2).
329|- **Cost.** Muse Spark is billed against the $150 credit on this account (D2: about $0.08 per investigation at ~120k input tokens, ~70% cached). Baseten, Modal and Fireworks each offer $100 to select participants for open-weights models.

Read text file `prompts/investigate.md`.
1|# Investigating an incident
2|
3|You are the site reliability engineer for a multi-tenant Google SecOps SOAR fleet run by a managed security provider. Each service (for example, a connector that ingests alerts, or a job that syncs threat intelligence) is deployed once per tenant environment, and tripwires watch every deployment. A tripwire has fired on one deployment. You are investigating it.
4|
5|Your tools read; none of them changes anything. You finish by submitting a diagnosis: a fix for a human to approve, no action, or an escalation to a human. Checks built into the tools grade everything you record and submit, and refuse anything that breaks the rules below. A refusal is not a failure: read it, fix what it names, and continue.
6|
7|The first user message describes the incident: the deployment, the tripped tripwire and its definition, why it tripped, the log entries it tripped on, the resource names of the deployment's components, the other deployments of the same service (siblings), the current time, and your budgets.
8|
9|## How the loop works
10|
11|- Call exactly one tool in each response. A response without a tool call gets the reply "Plain text is not accepted. Call exactly one tool." as your next input, and still uses a turn. If a response contains more than one call, only the first runs.
12|- Every call takes `rationale`: one line of at most 200 characters saying what you expect to learn or decide with this call. It is the only part of your reasoning anyone reads.
13|- Budgets: the turns, read calls and tokens named in the incident message. The eight read tools count as reads; `set_hypotheses`, `update_plan`, `record_evidence` and `submit_diagnosis` do not. A read past the cap is refused. Using up the tokens without an accepted submission pauses the investigation. A refused call still uses a turn.
14|- Calling the same tool with the same arguments a third time pauses the investigation as stuck, before that call runs. Rewording `rationale` or reordering keys does not make a call different. If a call did not give you what you needed, change it or move on.
15|- When a message says this is your last turn, call `submit_diagnosis` with what you have.
16|- An investigation can pause for a human and resume later. The resume message says what changed. You keep your hypotheses and evidence, and you get more turns and 4 more read calls; the counts for repeated calls and refused submissions start again.
17|
18|## Workflow
19|
20|1. **`set_hypotheses` first.** Nothing can be recorded or submitted before it is accepted.
21|   - 2 to 4 hypotheses, with unique IDs `H1`, `H2`, and so on: `H` followed by a number, with no leading zero.
22|   - Each has a `statement` (the explanation) and `wouldConfirm` (what you would expect to find if it were true).
23|   - At least one is marked `alternative: true`: a competing explanation. A useful default is that the problem is fleet-wide or upstream, not specific to this tenant.
24|   - Calling `set_hypotheses` again replaces the set. Evidence recorded for an ID you drop is discarded.
25|2. **`update_plan`** (optional): how you will settle each hypothesis.
26|3. **Investigate** with the read tools. Record evidence as soon as you find it, not at the end.
27|4. **`submit_diagnosis`.**
28|
29|## Reading tool results
30|
31|Every result arrives as `{"callId": "...", "result": {...}}`. The `callId` is what you cite when you record evidence from that result.
32|
33|A refused call returns `{"callId": "...", "result": {"error": "...", "problems": ["..."]}}`. Each problem starts with the rule it broke, for example `evidence.value: ...`. Fix exactly what `problems` names. Do not resend the same call unchanged.
34|
35|## Recording evidence
36|

9|    from fleetsre.contracts import Contract

13|@dataclass(frozen=True)
14|class Deployment:
15|    """A service applied to one environment, with parameters from fleet.yaml."""
16|
17|    id: str
18|    service: str
19|    environment: str
20|    parameters: dict[str, Any]
21|    resources: Mapping[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
22|
23|
24|def deployments_from_fleet(
25|    fleet: "FleetConfig",
26|    contract: "Contract",
27|    environments: Sequence[str] | None = None,
28|) -> list[Deployment]:
29|    """Build armed deployments for a service from a loaded fleet.
30|
31|    Parameters come from the fleet's deployment entries. ``resources``
32|    maps component id to the fleet's resource instance id, matched by
33|    component kind (connectorInstance -> connectorInstance,
34|    jobInstance -> jobInstance); components without a fleet instance id
35|    (e.g. ETL flows) have no entry.
36|    """
37|    if environments is None:
38|        envs = sorted(
39|            env
40|            for env, spec in fleet.environments.items()
41|            if contract.service in spec.deployments
42|        )
43|    else:
44|        envs = list(environments)
45|    deployments: list[Deployment] = []
46|    for env in envs:
47|        dep = fleet.environments[env].deployments[contract.service]
48|        resources: dict[str, str] = {}
49|        for component in contract.components:
50|            if (
51|                component.kind == "connectorInstance"
52|                and dep.connectorInstance
53|            ):
54|                resources[component.id] = dep.connectorInstance
55|            elif component.kind == "jobInstance" and dep.jobInstance:
56|                resources[component.id] = dep.jobInstance
57|        deployments.append(
58|            Deployment(
59|                id=f"{contract.service}/{env}",
60|                service=contract.service,
61|                environment=env,
62|                parameters=dict(dep.parameters),
63|                resources=resources,
64|            )
65|        )
66|    return deployments

1|"""D2 SRE feasibility spike.
2|
3|Interface (docs/deliverables.md §D2):
4|  python spikes/sre_spike.py --fixture <dir> [--model {scripted|<model id>}]
5|      [--runs N] [--gates on|off] [--script <file>]
6|
7|--model defaults to $FLEETSRE_SPIKE_MODEL, else muse-spark-1.3.
8|--script defaults to <fixture>/scripted.json.
9|Stdout per run: one TRACE line per turn, then RESULT, then DIAGNOSIS if accepted.
10|RESULT is {"run","status","turns","readCalls","refusals","multiCallTurns"}:
11|"status" is "accepted" iff the run ends with an accepted submission, and
12|"multiCallTurns" counts turns whose model response held more than one
13|function_call (only the first call runs).
14|Exit 0 when the program completes, whatever the run outcomes.
15|
16|Stub tools read the fixture dir only. incident.json "now" is the current
17|time: no tool returns anything after it.
18|Read-tool result contracts:
19|  query_logs -> {"entries": [...], "total": int, "truncated": bool}
20|    At most 50 entries, newest first. "total" counts every match at or
21|    before incident now; entries after now never match. "truncated" is
22|    true when matches exceed 50. "deployment" matches
23|    jsonPayload.environment; "window" is a half-open "<start>/<end>" interval
24|    of ISO-8601 UTC instants; "filter" is "" (all), "severity >= WARNING",
25|    or "event = <jsonPayload.event>".
26|  get_resource -> the resource object exactly as in resources.json
27|  list_connector_logs -> {"logs": [...], "total": int, "truncated": bool}
28|    At most 50 records, newest first, mirroring the fixture order.
29|    Records with "time" (unix ms) after incident now are excluded;
30|    "total" counts the records at or before now.
31|  test_integration_instance -> {"success": bool, "message": str}
32|  compare_siblings -> {"window": str, "deployments": {deployment: signals}}
33|    "window" echoes the request. Per deployment of the service, computed
34|    from logs.jsonl over the window: {"runs": int, "warningRuns": int,
35|    "errorRuns": int, "alertsIngested": int, "lastRunAt": str}. "runs"
36|    counts connector.run.completed entries; warning/errorRuns count runs
37|    with a WARNING/ERROR entry; alertsIngested counts alert.ingested;
38|    lastRunAt is the newest completed timestamp. No verdict, only signals.
39|
40|Minimal gates (inside the working tools): hypotheses before evidence or
41|submission; 2-4 hypotheses with at least one alternative; a log source's
42|insertId exists; a tool source's callId is a call made in this run; cited
43|evidence IDs were recorded. A refused record_evidence call consumes no
44|evidence ID. A tool source's "field" is a dotted path into that call's
45|result (e.g. "deployments.alert-ingestion/alpha.warningRuns"); the gate
46|refuses when the path is missing or its value differs.
47|"""

123|    def query_logs(

127|        _ = rationale

133|        env = deployment.split("/", 1)[1] if "/" in deployment else deployment
134|        try:

146|                "problems": [filters_help],

148|        want_event = filter[len("event = "):] if filter.startswith("event = ") else None
149|        matched: list[dict] = []

3|Interface (docs/deliverables.md §D2):
4|  python spikes/sre_spike.py --fixture <dir> [--model {scripted|<model id>}]
5|      [--runs N] [--gates on|off] [--script <file>]
6|
7|--model defaults to $FLEETSRE_SPIKE_MODEL, else muse-spark-1.3.
8|--script defaults to <fixture>/scripted.json.
9|Stdout per run: one TRACE line per turn, then RESULT, then DIAGNOSIS if accepted.
10|RESULT is {"run","status","turns","readCalls","refusals","multiCallTurns"}:
11|"status" is "accepted" iff the run ends with an accepted submission, and
12|"multiCallTurns" counts turns whose model response held more than one
13|function_call (only the first call runs).
14|Exit 0 when the program completes, whatever the run outcomes.
15|
16|Stub tools read the fixture dir only. incident.json "now" is the current
17|time: no tool returns anything after it.
18|Read-tool result contracts:
19|  query_logs -> {"entries": [...], "total": int, "truncated": bool}
20|    At most 50 entries, newest first. "total" counts every match at or
21|    before incident now; entries after now never match. "truncated" is
22|    true when matches exceed 50. "deployment" matches
23|    jsonPayload.environment; "window" is a half-open "<start>/<end>" interval
24|    of ISO-8601 UTC instants; "filter" is "" (all), "severity >= WARNING",
25|    or "event = <jsonPayload.event>".
26|  get_resource -> the resource object exactly as in resources.json
27|  list_connector_logs -> {"logs": [...], "total": int, "truncated": bool}
28|    At most 50 records, newest first, mirroring the fixture order.
29|    Records with "time" (unix ms) after incident now are excluded;
30|    "total" counts the records at or before now.
31|  test_integration_instance -> {"success": bool, "message": str}
32|  compare_siblings -> {"window": str, "deployments": {deployment: signals}}
33|    "window" echoes the request. Per deployment of the service, computed
34|    from logs.jsonl over the window: {"runs": int, "warningRuns": int,
35|    "errorRuns": int, "alertsIngested": int, "lastRunAt": str}. "runs"
36|    counts connector.run.completed entries; warning/errorRuns count runs
37|    with a WARNING/ERROR entry; alertsIngested counts alert.ingested;
38|    lastRunAt is the newest completed timestamp. No verdict, only signals.
39|
40|Minimal gates (inside the working tools): hypotheses before evidence or
41|submission; 2-4 hypotheses with at least one alternative; a log source's
42|insertId exists; a tool source's callId is a call made in this run; cited
43|evidence IDs were recorded. A refused record_evidence call consumes no
44|evidence ID. A tool source's "field" is a dotted path into that call's

843|def _live_call_with_backoff(client: object, kwargs: dict) -> object:
844|    last_exc: Exception | None = None
845|    delay = 1.0
846|    for attempt in range(6):
847|        try:
848|            return client.responses.create(**kwargs)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
849|        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - SDK error types vary
850|            name = type(exc).__name__
851|            msg = str(exc)
852|            status = getattr(exc, "status_code", None)
853|            if status is None:
854|                status = getattr(getattr(exc, "response", None), "status_code", None)
855|            is_429 = status == 429 or "429" in name or "429" in msg or "RateLimit" in name
856|            last_exc = exc
857|            if not is_429 or attempt >= 5:
858|                raise
859|            time.sleep(delay)
860|            delay *= 2.0
861|    assert last_exc is not None
862|    raise last_exc

843|def _live_call_with_backoff(client: object, kwargs: dict) -> object:
844|    last_exc: Exception | None = None
845|    delay = 1.0
846|    for attempt in range(6):
847|        try:
848|            return client.responses.create(**kwargs)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
849|        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - SDK error types vary
850|            name = type(exc).__name__
851|            msg = str(exc)
852|            status = getattr(exc, "status_code", None)
853|            if status is None:
854|                status = getattr(getattr(exc, "response", None), "status_code", None)
855|            is_429 = status == 429 or "429" in name or "429" in msg or "RateLimit" in name
856|            last_exc = exc
857|            if not is_429 or attempt >= 5:
858|                raise
859|            time.sleep(delay)
860|            delay *= 2.0
861|    assert last_exc is not None
862|    raise last_exc

1|# Fleet SRE — Mock Inventory
2|
3|As of 2026-10-28. Companion to [`spec.md`](spec.md) (source of truth) and [`deliverables.md`](deliverables.md) (D3 builds everything here).
4|
5|Revised 2026-10-29 (night) before D3: Chronicle method bodies (§4.1), method permissions (§4.2) and connector log collection (§4.1) checked against Google's docs.
6|
7|The mock simulates only what the SRE, the evaluator and the executor touch. Everything below is either **faithful** (copied from Google's or Microsoft's published docs, with a URL) or **invented** (labelled, because the docs do not publish it). §9 lists which is which.
8|
9|---
10|
11|## 1. What is being simulated
12|
13|```
14|Fake Sentinel (one workspace per tenant) ──poll──▶ Connector runtime ──AlertInfo──▶ Ingestion (ETL)
15|        ▲                                               │                               │
16|        │ plant canary                                   ▼                               ▼
17|   Canary planter                              python-container logs           etl-container logs
18|                                                + ConnectorLog records          (correlation_id)
19|Fake TI feed ──▶ Job runtime (intel-sync) ──▶ python-container logs + JobInstanceLog records
20|
21|Mock Chronicle API (control plane): read, patch, run, test ◀── SRE read tools / Executor writes
22|Fault injector (/_chaos): changes world behaviour on a schedule or on request
23|```
24|
25|All of it runs in one Python process (`fleetsre.mock`), driven by a `World` object with an injectable `Clock` and a seeded RNG, so a scenario replays identically.
26|
27|## 2. Fleet
28|
29|| Environment | Display name | Services | Alert volume (`expectedAlertsPerHour`) | Notes |
30|| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
31|| `alpha` | Alpha Corp | alert-ingestion, intel-sync | 120 | High volume |
32|| `bravo` | Bravo Health | alert-ingestion, intel-sync | 30 | Medium |
33|| `charlie` | Charlie Retail | alert-ingestion | 2 | Deliberately quiet; a naive "no alerts in 90 min" detector false-alarms here |
34|| `canary` | MSSP Canary | alert-ingestion | 0 organic | MSSP-owned canary tenant (production canary story) |
35|
36|Connector `intervalSeconds`: 60 for all (demo speed). Job `intervalSeconds`: 300 (docs minimum is 60). Defined in `fixtures/fleet.yaml` (D1). Tenant names are fictional.
37|
38|## 3. Components
39|
40|### 3.1 Fake Sentinel (upstream, invented transport, faithful payload)
41|
42|One simulated workspace per environment. The connector polls it.
43|
44|- **Payload shape** follows Microsoft Sentinel *Incidents – List*: `value[]` of incidents with `name`, `etag`, `type: "Microsoft.SecurityInsights/incidents"`, and `properties` including `title`, `description`, `severity`, `status`, `incidentNumber`, `createdTimeUtc`, `firstActivityTimeUtc`, `lastActivityTimeUtc`, `lastModifiedTimeUtc`, `providerName`, `providerIncidentId`, `labels`, `additionalData.alertsCount`. [source](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/rest/api/securityinsights/incidents/list)
45|- **Severity values**: `High`, `Medium`, `Low`, `Informational`.
46|- **Path**: simplified to `/_upstream/{env}/incidents?since=<iso8601>` (invented). The real ARM path is not needed.
47|- **Auth**: fake token endpoint `/_upstream/{env}/token` taking a client secret; returns 401 when the credential fault is active (invented).
48|- **Volume**: Poisson arrivals at the environment's rate, seeded.
49|
50|### 3.2 Connector runtime (emulates the SOAR `python` container)
51|
52|One worker per connector instance. Every `intervalSeconds` (while `enabled` and not stalled):
53|
54|1. Get a token from the fake token endpoint using the instance's `Client Secret` parameter.
55|2. Fetch incidents since the stored checkpoint (dedupe by `providerIncidentId`).
56|3. Map each incident to an `AlertInfo` (faithful field names, [source](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/soar/respond/ide/creating-a-custom-connector)):
57|   - `name` ← `properties.title`
58|   - `ticket_id` / `display_id` ← `properties.providerIncidentId`
59|   - `rule_generator` ← first label or `"Sentinel Analytics"` (must not be empty)
60|   - `priority` ← severity map: `High→80`, `Medium→60`, `Low→40`, `Informational→-1` (Google's scale is Informative −1, Low 40, Medium 60, High 80, Critical 100)
61|   - unknown severity → the `Unknown Severity Priority` parameter if set, **otherwise the raw string is passed through** (this is the severity-drift bug)
62|   - `device_vendor = "Microsoft"`, `device_product = "Azure Sentinel"`
63|   - `start_time` / `end_time` ← first/last activity (unix ms)
64|   - `environment` ← the instance's environment
65|   - `events` ← one event dict per incident with `device_product`
66|4. Hand alerts to ingestion.
67|5. Emit logs (see §5) and, while log collection is on (§4.1), append `ConnectorLog` records. Every run ends with `connector.run.completed`, including a run that failed; a failed run writes `connector.run.warning` or `connector.run.error` first (invented). So `dead-connector` measures whether the connector ran, and `connector-errors` whether it ran cleanly.
68|
69|**Swallowed failure (Green Liar).** On a 401 from upstream, the worker catches the exception, writes a `WARNING` log (and, while log collection is on, a `WARNING` ConnectorLog) ("Failed to authenticate to Sentinel workspace: 401 Unauthorized"), returns zero alerts and still emits `connector.run.completed`. Status stays `LIVE`.
70|
71|**Custom connector definition (invented — not the Marketplace integration's real parameters).**
72|
73|| Integration | `MockSentinel` (custom: true), version `1.0` |
74|| --- | --- |
75|| Connector | `Mock Sentinel Incidents Connector` |
76|| `productFieldName` / `eventFieldName` | `device_product` / `event_name` |
77|
78|Connector instance parameters (`ConnectorInstanceParameter`: `value`, `displayName`, `description`, `mandatory`, `advanced`, `type`):
79|
80|| displayName | type | mandatory | default |
81|| --- | --- | --- | --- |
82|| Tenant ID | STRING | yes | per env |
83|| Client ID | STRING | yes | per env |
84|| Client Secret | PASSWORD | yes | per env |
85|| Workspace Name | STRING | yes | per env |
86|| Max Incidents Per Cycle | INT | no | `50` |
87|| Unknown Severity Priority | INT | no | `""` (empty) |
88|
89|### 3.3 Ingestion (emulates the SOAR `etl` container)
90|
91|Receives `AlertInfo` objects. For each: assign a `correlation_id` (UUID4 from the seeded RNG), emit one `etl` log entry `alert.ingested` with the alert in `jsonPayload.alert` (fields: `name`, `ticket_id`, `rule_generator`, `priority`, `device_vendor`, `device_product`, `environment`, `start_time`, `end_time`, `canary`). 95|### 3.4 Job runtime (intel-sync)
96|
97|One worker per job instance. Every `intervalSeconds`: fetch indicators from a fake TI feed (`/_upstream/{env}/indicators?lookbackHours=N`), "sync" them, write a `python` log entry `job.run.completed` with `jsonPayload.indicatorsSynced` and `jsonPayload.status`, and append a `JobInstanceLog` (`status` `SUCCESS`/`ERROR`, `message`, `startTime`, `endTime`). Updates the job instance's `lastRunTime`, `lastRunStatus`, `nextScheduledRunTime`. A failed run writes `job.run.error` and then still ends with `job.run.completed` (`status: ERROR`, `indicatorsSynced: 0`, severity ERROR), so `dead-job` measures whether the job ran and `hollow-run` checks only `SUCCESS` runs (invented).
98|
99|Job definition (invented): integration `MockThreatIntel` v`1.0`, job `Sync Indicators`. Parameters:
100|
101|| displayName | type | mandatory | default |
102|| --- | --- | --- | --- |
103|| Feed URL | URL | yes | `/_upstream/{env}/indicators` |
104|| Lookback Hours | INT | yes | `24` |
105|
106|`Lookback Hours = 0` returns zero indicators with status `SUCCESS` (the hollow-success bug).
107|
108|### 3.5 Canary planter
109|
110|`POST /_upstream/{env}/incidents:plant` creates an incident whose title starts with `[CANARY]` and whose `providerIncidentId` is `canary-<uuid>`. Ingestion sets `jsonPayload.alert.canary = true` for it. A canary counts as seen when an `alert.ingested` entry has `alert.canary: true` and `alert.ticket_id` equal to the planted `providerIncidentId`. Canaries are planted with severity `Informational`, so F3 never affects them. The platform's synthetic tripwire calls this endpoint; in production it would target only the `canary` environment (spec §5).

185|## 5. Log format
186|
187|Every log line, local or in Cloud Logging, is a Cloud Logging `LogEntry`:
188|
189|```json
190|{
191|  "insertId": "a1b2c3d4e5",
192|  "timestamp": "2026-10-29T14:00:05.123Z",
193|  "severity": "WARNING",
194|  "logName": "projects/fleet-sre-demo/logs/chronicle-soar",
195|  "resource": {
196|    "type": "k8s_container",
197|    "labels": {
198|      "project_id": "fleet-sre-demo",
199|      "location": "us-central1",
200|      "cluster_name": "mock-soar",
201|      "namespace_name": "chronicle-soar",
202|      "pod_name": "python-0",
203|      "container_name": "python"
204|    }
205|  },
206|  "labels": {
207|    "integration_name": "MockSentinel",
208|    "integration_version": "1.0",
209|    "connector_name": "Mock Sentinel Incidents Connector",
210|    "connector_instance": "alpha-sentinel"
211|  },
212|  "jsonPayload": {
213|    "event": "connector.run.completed",
214|    "runId": "run-000123",
215|    "environment": "alpha",
216|    "alertsFetched": 0,
217|    "message": "Failed to authenticate to Sentinel workspace: 401 Unauthorized"
218|  }
219|}
220|```
221|
222|Faithful: `namespace_name = "chronicle-soar"`, `container_name` ∈ {`playbook`, `python`, `etl`}, and the entry `labels`: connector logs carry `integration_name`, `integration_version`, `connector_name`, `connector_instance`; job logs carry `integration_name`, `integration_version`, `job_name`; etl logs carry `correlation_id`. [source](https://docs.cloud.google.com/chronicle/docs/secops/collect-secops-soar-logs)

224|Invented: `logName`, `pod_name`, `cluster_name`, every `jsonPayload` field, and the `event` names below.
225|
226|| `event` | Container | Labels | Key payload fields |
227|| --- | --- | --- | --- |
228|| `connector.run.started` | python | connector | `runId`, `environment` |
229|| `connector.run.completed` | python | connector | `runId`, `alertsFetched`, `environment` |
230|| `connector.run.warning` | python | connector | `runId`, `message` (severity WARNING) |
231|| `connector.run.error` | python | connector | `runId`, `message` (severity ERROR) |

242|## 6. Fault catalog
243|
244|Each fault has a defined cause, what the native API shows, what should trip, and the **right answer**: the action a correct SRE takes. The right answers make the evaluations gradeable.
245|
246|| ID | Fault | Mock behaviour | Native API shows | Should trip | Right answer |
247|| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
248|| F1 | `connector_stall` | Worker for one instance stops running. No logs, no ConnectorLogs | `status: LIVE`, `enabled: true` | `dead-connector` (cadence) | `connectorInstances.restart`. The mock clears a stall on any `enabled` false→true transition |
249|| F2 | `credential_expiry` | Upstream token endpoint returns 401 for one env. Connector swallows it: WARNING logs every run (and WARNING ConnectorLogs while log collection is on), zero alerts, runs on schedule | `status: LIVE`; `executeTest` → `successful: false`; the Logs tab is empty unless log collection is on | `connector-errors` (errorSignature), `canary` (synthetic) | `escalate`, category `credential_failure`. Siblings healthy → tenant-specific. Fix (rotate secret) is outside the allowlist |
250|| F3 | `severity_drift` | A fraction `rate` (fault `params`, e.g. 0.5) of new upstream incidents arrive with an unmapped severity (`"Critical"`); with `Unknown Severity Priority` empty, their `priority` becomes a string | `status: LIVE`, volume normal | `priority-shape` (schema) | `connectorInstances.patch` `parameters`: set `Unknown Severity Priority` to `100` (or `80`) |
251|| F4 | `job_hollow_success` | Job parameter `Lookback Hours` set to `0` (simulates a bad config change, visible in `tripwire_history` as a recent change); runs succeed with 0 indicators. Injection sets the parameter through the same path as a patch (bumps `updateTime`); `clear()` restores the value it replaced | `lastRunStatus: SUCCESS` | intel-sync `hollow-run` (schema on `indicatorsSynced > 0` over N runs) | `jobInstances.patch` `parameters`: `Lookback Hours` → `24` |
252|| F5 | `job_error` | Fake TI feed returns 500; job runs end `ERROR` | `lastRunStatus: ERROR` | intel-sync `job-errors` (errorSignature) | `escalate`, category `job_failing` (upstream outage) |
253|| F6 | `connector_flap` | Instance emits ERROR on a fraction `rate` of runs (fault `params`, e.g. 0.2 or 0.7). ERROR runs still fetch and ingest normally | `status: LIVE` | `connector-errors` only if threshold met | Harness-only scenarios for false-positive and threshold tuning |
254|| F7 | `job_stall` | Job worker stops running; `nextScheduledRunTime` goes stale | `lastRunStatus` unchanged, `enabled: true` | intel-sync `dead-job` (cadence) | `jobInstances.restart`, category `job_stalled`. The mock clears a job stall on any `enabled` false→true transition |
255|
256|Clearing: `DELETE /_chaos/faults/{id}` restores normal behaviour within 2 intervals. F2 has no allowlisted fix; in the demo, the admin UI "mark rotated" button clears it.

258|## 7. Chaos API
259|
260|Enabled only when `FLEETSRE_CHAOS=1`; otherwise every `/_chaos` route returns 404.
261|
262|| Method | Path | Body | Effect |
263|| --- | --- | --- | --- |
264|| `POST` | `/_chaos/faults` | `{"type": "severity_drift", "environment": "alpha", "target": "<resource name, optional>", "params": {"rate": 0.5}}` | Activates a fault; returns `{"id": "..."}` |
265|| `GET` | `/_chaos/faults` | | Active faults |
266|| `DELETE` | `/_chaos/faults/{id}` | | Clears a fault |
267|| `POST` | `/_chaos/schedule` | list of `{at, type, environment, params?, clearAt?}` | Scenario schedule (harness and the live auto-chaos loop) |
268|
269|## 8. Determinism and time
270|
271|- `World(seed, clock, sink, fleet)`; `world.step_until(t)` advances a `SimClock` and runs every due worker in timestamp order.
272|- Same seed + same fleet + same fault schedule → byte-identical JSONL.
273|- Wall-clock mode (`world.run_forever()`) is used for the live demo only.
274|
275|## 9. Faithful versus invented
276|
277|| Faithful (cite in code comments) | Invented (say so in the README) |
278|| --- | --- |
279|| Resource names, paths, methods and field lists (§4.1) | Fake Sentinel transport and token endpoint |
280|| `status` enum values, `logLevel` and `JobResultStatus` enums, `ParamType` enum | Meaning of `LIVE` (mock rule in §4.1) |
281|| `integrationVersion` required on connector patch; job `intervalSeconds` minimum 60 | Collection captures all log levels |
282|| Method request and response bodies: `executeTest`, `runOnDemand`, `setLogsCollection` | `runOnDemand` ignoring the body's values |
283|| ConnectorLogs collected only during a 3-hour collection period; enabling clears existing records | PASSWORD round-trip on patch |
284|| Permission name pattern and the method permissions in §4.2 | The two permission deviations in §4.2 |
285|| Log namespace, containers and entry labels (§5) | `logName`, `pod_name`, every `jsonPayload` field, event names |
286|| AlertInfo field names and the priority scale | The custom connector's and job's parameters |
287|| Sentinel incident payload fields and severities | Fault mechanics (§6) |

"""Generate fixtures/scripted/{F1,F2,F3,F4,F5,F7}.json from seeded worlds.

Each fixture is {fault, seed, t0, faults, incident, responses} where
responses are Responses API outputs (output arrays with usage) for a good
investigation. Cited insertIds and tool values come from the seeded world;
incident deployments/tripwires are the pinned D5 set; fault types, seeds,
at offsets and withinSeconds are derived from the scenario that expects
the same tripwire.

import argparse

import json
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
T0 = datetime(2026, 10, 29, 14, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)

# Pinned D5 incidents: fault -> (deployment, tripwire).
PINNED = {
    "F1": ("alert-ingestion/alpha", "dead-connector"),
    "F2": ("alert-ingestion/bravo", "connector-errors"),
    "F3": ("alert-ingestion/alpha", "priority-shape"),
    "F4": ("intel-sync/alpha", "hollow-run"),
    "F5": ("intel-sync/bravo", "job-errors"),
    "F7": ("intel-sync/alpha", "dead-job"),
}

# Right-answer categories per mocks.md §6 (test expectation, not world data).
CATEGORY = {
    "F1": "connector_stalled",
    "F2": "credential_failure",
    "F3": "schema_drift",
    "F4": "job_hollow_success",
    "F5": "job_failing",
    "F7": "job_stalled",
}


# Fault types per mocks.md §6 (setup input; seeds/offsets still derived).
FAULT_TYPE = {
    "F1": "connector_stall",
    "F2": "credential_expiry",
    "F3": "severity_drift",
    "F4": "job_hollow_success",
    "F5": "job_error",
    "F7": "job_stall",
}


def _load_scenario_for_fault(fault: str, tripwire: str) -> Any:
    from fleetsre.harness.scenario import load_scenario

    want = FAULT_TYPE[fault]
    fallback = None
    for path in sorted((ROOT / "fixtures" / "scenarios").rglob("*.yaml")):
        scenario = load_scenario(path)
        trips = [t.tripwire for t in scenario.expected.trips]
        if tripwire not in trips:
            continue
        if not scenario.faults or scenario.faults[0].type != want:
            continue
        if scenario.faults[0].clearAt is None:
            return scenario
        fallback = scenario
    if fallback is not None:
        return fallback
    raise AssertionError(f"no scenario for {fault} {tripwire!r}")


def _trip_until(
    world: Any, evaluator: Any, clock: Any, sink: Any,
    deployment: str, tripwire: str,
) -> Any:
    consumed = 0
    tick = 15
    elapsed = 0
    while elapsed <= 24 * 3600:
        tick_at = T0 + timedelta(seconds=elapsed)
        clock.set(tick_at)
        world.step_until(tick_at)
        events: list[Any] = []
        while consumed < len(sink.entries):
            events.extend(evaluator.ingest(sink.entries[consumed]))
            consumed += 1
        events.extend(evaluator.tick())
        for event in events:
            if (
                event.kind == "trip"
                and event.deployment == deployment
                and event.tripwire == tripwire
            ):
                clock.set(event.at)
                return event
        elapsed += tick
    raise AssertionError(f"no trip for {deployment} {tripwire}")

58|def schema_violation(entry: LogEntry, spec: SchemaSpec) -> str | None:
59|    """Reason when entry violates the schema spec, else None.
60|
61|    Entries whose event or ``where`` filters do not match are not
62|    applicable and return None (the engine ignores them entirely).
63|    """

66|            return None

68|        for key, want in spec.where.items():
69|            found, value = _lookup(entry, key)
70|            if not found or value != want:

73|    if not found or value is None:
74|        if spec.required:
75|            return f"missing required field {spec.field}"
76|        return None
77|    if spec.type == "integer":
78|        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
79|            return f"field {spec.field} is not an integer: {value!r}"
80|    elif spec.type == "number":
81|        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
82|            return f"field {spec.field} is not a number: {value!r}"
83|    elif spec.type == "string":
84|        if not isinstance(value, str):
85|            return f"field {spec.field} is not a string: {value!r}"
86|    elif spec.type == "boolean":
87|        if not isinstance(value, bool):
88|            return f"field {spec.field} is not a boolean: {value!r}"
89|    else:
90|        return f"unknown schema type {spec.type!r} for field {spec.field}"
91|    if spec.enum is not None and value not in spec.enum:
92|        return f"field {spec.field} value {value!r} not in {list(spec.enum)!r}"
93|    if spec.minimum is not None and isinstance(value, (int, float)):
94|        if value < spec.minimum:
95|            return (
96|                f"field {spec.field} value {value!r} "
97|                f"below minimum {spec.minimum!r}"
98|            )

102|def error_signature(
103|    recent_run_severities: Sequence[str], spec: ErrorSigSpec
104|) -> bool:
105|    """True when WARNING-or-worse runs in the window reach threshold.
106|
107|    Only the last ``windowRuns`` entries count; a run counts when its
108|    severity is at or above ``minSeverity``.
109|    """
110|    order = _SEVERITY_ORDER.get(spec.minSeverity, 0)
111|    window = list(recent_run_severities)[-spec.windowRuns :]
112|    bad = sum(1 for sev in window if _SEVERITY_ORDER.get(sev, -1) >= order)

23|def cadence_due(
24|    last_event_at: datetime | None,
25|    armed_at: datetime,
26|    now: datetime,
27|    interval_s: int,
28|    max_silent: int,
29|) -> bool:

38|def _lookup(entry: LogEntry, dotted: str) -> tuple[bool, Any]:
39|    """Look up a dotted field path rooted at the entry.
40|
41|    Returns (found, value). ``jsonPayload`` addresses the payload dict;
42|    ``labels`` and ``resource.labels`` address the label maps.
43|    """
44|    parts = dotted.split(".")
45|    node: Any = {
46|        "jsonPayload": entry.jsonPayload,
47|        "labels": entry.labels,
48|        "resource": {"labels": entry.resource.labels},
49|    }
50|    for part in parts:
51|        if isinstance(node, dict) and part in node:
52|            node = node[part]
53|        else:
54|            return False, None
55|    return True, node

58|def schema_violation(entry: LogEntry, spec: SchemaSpec) -> str | None:
59|    """Reason when entry violates the schema spec, else None.
60|
61|    Entries whose event or ``where`` filters do not match are not
62|    applicable and return None (the engine ignores them entirely).
63|    """
64|    if spec.event is not None:
65|        if entry.jsonPayload.get("event") != spec.event:
66|            return None
67|    if spec.where:
68|        for key, want in spec.where.items():
69|            found, value = _lookup(entry, key)
70|            if not found or value != want:
71|                return None
72|    found, value = _lookup(entry, spec.field)
73|    if not found or value is None:
74|        if spec.required:
75|            return f"missing required field {spec.field}"
76|        return None
77|    if spec.type == "integer":
78|        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
79|            return f"field {spec.field} is not an integer: {value!r}"
80|    elif spec.type == "number":
81|        if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
82|            return f"field {spec.field} is not a number: {value!r}"
83|    elif spec.type == "string":
84|        if not isinstance(value, str):
85|            return f"field {spec.field} is not a string: {value!r}"
86|    elif spec.type == "boolean":
87|        if not isinstance(value, bool):
88|            return f"field {spec.field} is not a boolean: {value!r}"
89|    else:
90|        return f"unknown schema type {spec.type!r} for field {spec.field}"
91|    if spec.enum is not None and value not in spec.enum:
92|        return f"field {spec.field} value {value!r} not in {list(spec.enum)!r}"
93|    if spec.minimum is not None and isinstance(value, (int, float)):
94|        if value < spec.minimum:
95|            return (
96|                f"field {spec.field} value {value!r} "
97|                f"below minimum {spec.minimum!r}"
98|            )
99|    return None

102|def error_signature(
103|    recent_run_severities: Sequence[str], spec: ErrorSigSpec
104|) -> bool:
105|    """True when WARNING-or-worse runs in the window reach threshold.
106|
107|    Only the last ``windowRuns`` entries count; a run counts when its
108|    severity is at or above ``minSeverity``.
109|    """
110|    order = _SEVERITY_ORDER.get(spec.minSeverity, 0)
111|    window = list(recent_run_severities)[-spec.windowRuns :]
112|    bad = sum(1 for sev in window if _SEVERITY_ORDER.get(sev, -1) >= order)
113|    return bad >= spec.threshold

116|def canary_missed(
117|    planted_at: datetime,
118|    seen_at: datetime | None,
119|    now: datetime,
120|    deadline_s: int,
121|) -> bool:
122|    """True when the planted canary missed its deadline.
123|
124|    A canary seen at or before the deadline never misses, even late now;
125|    a canary seen after the deadline still missed.
126|    """
127|    if seen_at is not None:
128|        if (seen_at - planted_at).total_seconds() <= deadline_s:
129|            return False
130|        return (now - planted_at).total_seconds() > deadline_s
131|    return (now - planted_at).total_seconds() > deadline_s

208|def _verify_seconds(
209|    contract: Any, tripwire: Any, parameters: dict[str, Any],
210|    sink_entries: list[Any], env: str, trip_at: datetime,
211|) -> int:
212|    """Recovery rule x1.5, rounded up to a minute (review pin 20)."""
213|    import math
214|
215|    def _resolve(value: Any) -> Any:
216|        if isinstance(value, str) and value.startswith("${"):
217|            return parameters[value[2:-1]]
218|        return value
219|
220|    spec = tripwire.spec
221|    base = 0.0
222|    if tripwire.type == "cadence":
223|        interval = int(_resolve(spec["intervalSeconds"]))
224|        base = float(2 * interval)
225|    elif tripwire.type == "errorSignature":
226|        interval = int(parameters["intervalSeconds"])
227|        window = int(_resolve(spec["windowRuns"]))
228|        threshold = int(_resolve(spec["threshold"]))
229|        base = float((window - threshold + 1) * interval + interval)
230|    else:
231|        recover_after = int(spec.get(
232|            "recoverAfter", spec.get("consecutive", 1)
233|        ))
234|        event = spec.get("event")
235|        count = sum(
236|            1 for e in sink_entries
237|            if e.jsonPayload.get("environment") == env
238|            and e.timestamp <= trip_at
239|            and (event is None or e.jsonPayload.get("event") == event)
240|        )
241|        duration = max((trip_at - T0).total_seconds(), 1)
242|        rate = count / duration
243|        base = recover_after / max(rate, 1e-9)
244|    return int(math.ceil(base * 1.5 / 60) * 60)

+    def route(self, entry: LogEntry) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:
+        """Route an entry to [(deployment ID, component ID)].

+        the component's container_name and match labels, then

+        Deployment.resources, with jsonPayload.environment as fallback.
+        """
+        found: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
+        container = entry.resource.labels.get("container_name")
+        for service, contract in self._contracts.items():

+                if component.logs.container_name != container:
+                    continue
+                if any(

+                    for key in component.logs.match
+                ):
+                    continue

+                    node = node[part]
+                else:

+            if not isinstance(node, str):
+                return None
+            dep_id = f"{service}/{node}"
+            return dep_id if dep_id in self._deployments else None

+        if not isinstance(env, str):

{"content":""""SQLite session store (local adapter for SessionStore)."""

import json
import sqlite3
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any


class SqliteSessionStore:
    """SessionStore backed by SQLite (spec.md §4.2)."""

    def __init__(self, path: str | Path) -> None:
        self._path = str(path)
        conn = sqlite3.connect(self._path)
        try:
            conn.execute(
                "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions ("
                "incident_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, data TEXT NOT NULL)"
            )
            conn.execute(
                "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS transcripts ("
                "transcript_id TEXT NOT NULL, seq INTEGER NOT NULL, "
                "record TEXT NOT NULL, "
                "PRIMARY KEY (transcript_id, seq))"
            )
            conn.commit()
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def _connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:
        return sqlite3.connect(self._path)

    def save(self, session: Any) -> None:
        from fleetsre.sre.session import Session

        if not isinstance(session, Session):
            session = Session.model_validate(session)
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT OR REPLACE INTO sessions (incident_id, data) "
                "VALUES (?, ?)",
                (session.incident_id, session.model_dump_json()),
            )
            conn.commit()
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def load(self, incident_id: str) -> Any:
        from fleetsre.sre.session import Session

        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT data FROM sessions WHERE incident_id = ?",
                (incident_id,),
            ).fetchone()
        finally:
            conn.close()
        if row is None:
            raise KeyError(f"unknown incident: {incident_id}")
        return Session.model_validate_json(row[0])

    def append_transcript(
        self, transcript_id: str, record: dict[str, Any]
    ) -> None:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq), -1) FROM transcripts "
                "WHERE transcript_id = ?",
                (transcript_id,),
            ).fetchone()
            seq = int(row[0]) + 1
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO transcripts (transcript_id, seq, record) "
                "VALUES (?, ?, ?)",
                (transcript_id, seq, json.dumps(record)),
            )
            conn.commit()
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def transcript(self, transcript_id: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        conn = self._connect()
        try:
            rows = conn.execute(
                "SELECT record FROM transcripts WHERE transcript_id = ? "
                "ORDER BY seq",
                (transcript_id,),
            ).fetchall()
        finally:
            conn.close()
        return [json.loads(row[0]) for row in rows]

{"content":"#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Record one live D5 investigation to fixtures/recorded/<FAULT>.json.

Rebuilds the scripted fixture's world, freezes it at the trip, runs one
live investigation, and writes {fault, seed, t0, faults, incident,
responses, transcript, diagnosis} (docs/d5-pins.md pin 32). Every
encrypted_content value is replaced with "<stripped>" at record time.

Usage: make record FAULT=<F1|F2|F3|F4|F5|F7>
Requires MODEL_API_KEY in the environment (never committed).
"""

import argparse
import copy
import json
import os
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT))

T0 = datetime(2026, 10, 29, 14, 0, 0, tzinfo=timezone.utc)


def _strip_encrypted(node: Any) -> Any:
    if isinstance(node, dict):
        return {
            key: "<stripped>" if key == "encrypted_content"
            else _strip_encrypted(value)
            for key, value in node.items()
        }
    if isinstance(node, list):
        return [_strip_encrypted(value) for value in node]
    return node


class RecordingTransport:
    """Wraps a transport, keeping deep copies of each model response."""

    def __init__(self, inner: Any) -> None:
        self._inner = inner
        self.responses: list[dict[str, Any]] = []

    def create(self, request: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        response = self._inner.create(request)
        self.responses.append(copy.deepcopy(response))
        return response


def _live_config() -> tuple[Any, str]:
    from fleetsre.sre.gateway import GatewayConfig, RoleConfig

    model = os.environ.get(
        "FLEETSRE_INVESTIGATE_MODEL", "muse-spark-1.3"
    )
    prices: dict[str, dict[str, float]] = {
        model: {"input": 0.0, "cached_input": 0.0, "output": 0.0}
    }
    raw = os.environ.get("FLEETSRE_PRICES_JSON", "")
    if raw:
        try:
            data = json.loads(raw)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            data = None
        if isinstance(data, dict):
            if model in data and isinstance(data[model], dict):
                prices = {model: dict(data[model])}
            elif "input" in data and "output" in data:
                prices = {model: dict(data)}
    return (
        GatewayConfig(
            roles={"investigate": RoleConfig(
                model=model, reasoning_effort="medium"
            )},
            base_url="https://api.meta.ai/v1",
            max_retries=5,
            prices=prices,
        ),
        model,
    )


def _trip_until(
    world: Any, evaluator: Any, clock: Any, sink: Any,
    deployment: str, tripwire: str,
) -> Any:
    consumed = 0
    elapsed = 0
    while elapsed <= 24 * 3600:
        tick_at = T0 + timedelta(seconds=elapsed)
        clock.set(tick_at)
        world.step_until(tick_at)
        events: list[Any] = []
        while consumed < len(sink.entries):
            events.extend(evaluator.ingest(sink.entries[consumed]))
            consumed += 1
        events.extend(evaluator.tick())
        for event in events:
            if (
                event.kind == "trip"
                and event.deployment == deployment
                and event.tripwire == tripwire
            ):
                clock.set(event.at)
                return event
        elapsed += 15
    raise AssertionError(f"no trip for {deployment} {tripwire}")


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

    from fleetsre.adapters.chronicle_http import ChronicleHttpClient
    from fleetsre.clock import SimClock
    from fleetsre.contracts import load_contract
    from fleetsre.evaluator.engine import Evaluator
    from fleetsre.mock.chronicle_api import create_app
    from fleetsre.mock.fleet import load_fleet
    from fleetsre.mock.world import World
    from fleetsre.ports import MemoryLogQuery, MemorySink, MemoryStateStore
    from fleetsre.registry import Registry, deployments_from_fleet
    from fleetsre.sre.gateway import (
        ModelGateway,
        OpenAITransport,
    )
    from fleetsre.sre.investigator import investigate
    from fleetsre.sre.schemas import Incident
    from fleetsre.sre.session import MemorySessionStore
    from fleetsre.sre.tools import ToolSet

    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Record a live D5 run")
    parser.add_argument("--fault", required=True,
                        help="fault ID, e.g. F1")
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    api_key = os.environ.get("MODEL_API_KEY", "")
    if not api_key:
        print("MODEL_API_KEY is not set; refusing a live run",
              file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    fixture_path = ROOT / "fixtures" / "scripted" / f"{args.fault}.json"
    fixture = json.loads(fixture_path.read_text())
    deployment = fixture["incident"]["deployment"]
    service = deployment.split("/", 1)[0]

    fleet = load_fleet(ROOT / "fixtures" / "fleet.yaml")
    contract = load_contract(ROOT / "contracts" / f"{service}.json")
    clock = SimClock(T0)
    sink = MemorySink()
    world = World(fleet, fixture["seed"], clock, sink)
    world.schedule(fixture["faults"])
    deployments = deployments_from_fleet(fleet, contract)
    evaluator = Evaluator([contract], deployments, clock)
    trip = _trip_until(
        world, evaluator, clock, sink, deployment,
        fixture["incident"]["tripwire"],
    )
    registry = Registry([contract], deployments)
    incident = Incident.from_trip(trip, registry, clock.now())

    log_query = MemoryLogQuery(sink)
    http = TestClient(create_app(world, dev_auth=True))
    chronicle = ChronicleHttpClient(http, "obs-reader")
    state = MemoryStateStore()
    tools = ToolSet(
        log_query, chronicle, state, registry,
        clock=clock, verification=True,
    )
    config, model = _live_config()
    recording = RecordingTransport(OpenAITransport(
        api_key=api_key, base_url="https://api.meta.ai/v1",
    ))
    gateway = ModelGateway(config, recording)
    store = MemorySessionStore()
    result = investigate(
        incident, tools, gateway, store, max_turns=24,
        max_read_calls=12, max_tokens=400_000,
    )
    payload = {
        "fault": args.fault,
        "seed": fixture["seed"],
        "t0": fixture["t0"],
        "faults": fixture["faults"],
        "incident": incident.model_dump(mode="json"),
        "responses": recording.responses,
        "transcript": store.transcript(result.transcript_id),
        "diagnosis": result.diagnosis,
    }
    payload = _strip_encrypted(payload)
    out_dir = ROOT / "fixtures" / "recorded"
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out_path = out_dir / f"{args.fault}.json"
    out_path.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2) + "\n")
    category = (result.diagnosis or {}).get("category", None)
    print(f"model: {model}")
    print(f"status: {result.status} reason: {result.reason}")
    print(f"turns: {result.turns} read_calls: {result.read_calls}")
    print(f"category: {category}")
    print(f"wrote {out_path}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
